title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: policy alert improvements
notes: claim 56: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the default-state field says Microsoft has not stated a default, although its notice explicitly says the feature is available by default. Published Communication Compliance licensing should be distinguished from any unpublished additional requirements, and existing policies should not be presented as a prerequisite for controls offered during policy creation.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence for this feature.
claims.quote: | Communication Compliance | Included | Included | Included | Included |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included" and replace the unqualified unpublished-licensing statements with: "Communication Compliance is included in eligible subscriptions, including Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 and Office 365 E5/A5/G5. No separate additional licensing requirement for these alert improvements is documented as of November 2026." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-communications-compliance. claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Alerts notify reviewers of policy matches for human investigation and subsequent action.
claims.quote: Review alerts to investigate detected messages and take action: Identify and analyze messages that match a policy's conditions to trigger alerts that provide context around a policy violation, so you can investigate and take action if needed.

claims.claim: No autonomous remediation action is described for the alert improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: communication compliance alert improvements new alerts page frequency recipients enable disable role license; read MC920304 and the roadmap description. Neither assigns remediation actions to the new alert settings.

claims.claim: Existing Communication Compliance policies are a prerequisite for the alert improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "existing policies" "alert frequency"; "Communication Compliance" "alert improvements" "employees" "prerequisites". Read MC920304 and configure: the new settings are described within policy creation, not as requiring pre-existing policies.
claims.fix: Remove "Existing Communication Compliance policies." from Prerequisites. In the risk rationale replace "for policies that already exist" with "per policy"; the notice places the settings in the policy creation wizard and does not establish a pre-existing-policy prerequisite.

claims.claim: The sources do not establish that the new alerts page replaces the existing alert policy trigger controls.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "existing policies" "alert frequency"; communication compliance alert improvements new alerts page frequency recipients enable disable role license. Read MC920304 and policies; neither describes replacement of the existing trigger controls.

claims.claim: Employees whose messages are inspected see nothing change.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "alert improvements" "employees" "prerequisites"; read MC920304, policies and configure. None guarantees that inspected employees see no change from the alert improvements.
claims.fix: Remove "employees whose messages are inspected see nothing change" from the impact rationale. Retain the assessment that the people directly using the settings are administrators and alert recipients.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls that are not represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Confirm who is in the Communication Compliance Admins role group" and "Set frequency and recipients per policy". Table rows: existing alert policy triggers; tenant-wide switch.
claims.fix: The role-group membership check and the per-policy alert-frequency/recipient configuration step have no corresponding controls-table rows. The existing-trigger row explicitly says it is not the new alerts page.
